## 1.3 Executive Summary
R
M
On 12 December 2020, Cairo North Power Plant started a planned Major Inspection (MI) for 
GT unit serial number 298464 and Generator 337X581 rotor out. 
GT:
Upon visual inspections and compressor mapping, findings were as follows:
1.      High corrosion pitting on compressor forward stages 0-5 (rotor and stator).
2.      R1-B28 with a dent with high risk of failure.
## 3.      Rust between the stators and casing on almost all stages causing difficult removal of
stators.
4.      Tip rubs and edge damages on several stages at random.
Recommendation was to replace stators and rotor per ER case and findings to reduce the 
risk of failure due to the as found condition.
Disassembly of all components started on 12 December 2020, new HGP components were 
reassembled, and team demobilized on 17 January 2021 until new compressor stator 
(Package 5) parts arrival.
Team returned on 22 January 2021 to install new upgraded Package 5 stators and IGV 
parts. All upper half casings were reinstalled to avoid casing deformation.
The scope was put on-hold on 12 February 2021 where site team demobilized until rotor 
repair and return for reassembly. The damaged rotor was placed inside the shipping box on 
13 February to be ready for shipping.
The team returned on June 15 for the reassembly phase, new rotor was received from 
Nubaria Power Plant.
The new turbine rotor was installed and all combustion and HGP components were replaced 
with new/refurbished parts. GT lift oil flow control valves were replaced with new ones.
The lube oil tank was cleaned by the customer, and placed new oil into the tank.
Generator:
The generator field was planned for repair, the unit was disassembled, and the field was 
pulled out on 1 January 2021 and ready for shipping. The rotor was lifted and sent for 
shipment on 22 January 2021 due to delay of shipping arrangements. The stator and 
removed parts were tested and visually inspected, and ER case called for stator re-wedge.
GT and generator parts (bearings/buckets/new CI components, end shields, special tools 
etc.) were stored by the customer until return of the both rotors.
Upon stator re-wedge parts arrival, scope was implemented successfully and electrical 
testing was performed before and after the scope as documented in the below report to 
GE Power   Power Services

## 1.3 Executive Summary
R
M
assess the condition of the generator prior to startup.
Preparation/Timeline of Events:
- The team started to Mobilize / Move on Site on 12th of December 2020.
- Team demobilized on 17th of January 2021 after disassembly.
- Team mobilized again on 22nd of January 2021 for generator rotor shipping, installing new 
Package 5 parts, and boxing up unit without the rotor to avoid any deformation/damage due 
to weather.
- Team demobilized on 14th of February after placing the old GT rotor in shipping box, and 
completing site cleanup.
- Team re-mobilized to site on 15th of June 2021 for GT reassembly and Generator re-wedge 
scopes.
- Team demobilized 15th of July awaiting missing re-wedge parts/chemicals (stuck in 
customs clearance).
- Team re-mobilized to site on 12th of August to finalize Generator re-wedge scope, 
mechanical reassembly and startup of the unit.
- Unit started up successfully on 4th of September, reaching a baseload of 235 MW. 
Emissions tuning was also performed on the unit.
GE/FieldCore team provided technical direction and supervision of all the mechanical 
activities throughout the outage. The scope of work is documented throughout this report. 
The unit is operated and maintained by the customer. The craft labor was provided by 
customer.
All the electrical connections and mechanical equipment etc. necessary to complete the 
work safely under the LOTO procedure were disconnected/isolated by GE and the permit to 
work system was implemented. All components that were removed and replaced have been 
documented in this report.
The following components were replaced with new and refurbished sets during the outage:
1.      Fuel nozzles and liner caps.
2.      Combustion liners and inner crossfire tubes.
3.      Transition pieces.
4.      1st, 2nd and 3rd stage nozzles.
5.      1st, 2nd and 3rd stage shrouds.
6.      1st, 2nd and 3rd stage buckets.
7.      IGV blades, arm and actuator (package 5 upgrade).
8.      Compressor stator vanes (package 5 upgrade).
9.      Unit rotor.
10.    Bearings (GT bearing 2 oversized).
11.    GT lift oil hoses and flow control valves.

### 3.10.2 Inlet Filter House
R
M
Part Condition: Good
Part Description: 
The filter house stripped down of old filters, cleaned and reassembled with new cylindrical 
and conical filters. Upon closeout inspection, minor damage to sheet metal on filters were 
noted and some mixed-and-matched elements from different manufacturers or batches of 
production. Comments on inadequate sealing have been corrected prior to operation.
The silencer duct and inlet plenum were entered for final inspection, noting clean and dry 
surfaces, intact probes, properly sealed expansion joints, and unchipped paint. Stud 
protrusion beyond the nut for the expansion joints were less than ideal, some just at the 
surface of the nut. The customer was advised to revise the quality and proper fill of the 
expansion joint on both the C-wall and air cone sides.

### 3.10.3 Turning Gear
R
M
Part Description: 
The turning gear and SSS clutch assembly was decoupled, preserved, and returned to 
position. The axial location was marked with stoppers welded on the base plate in lieu of 
drilling new dowel pins.
Recommendation Status: Should be planned for next Outage
Recommendation Type: Parts
Recommendation Description: 
The turning gear assembly is one of the most important components of the GT train and is 
necessary for operation, particularly during startup and shutdown. Normal wear and age 
may soon affect the integrity of the system. The customer is recommended to have in store 
replacement parts for the worm gear, ratcheting device, SSS clutch, or the assembly as a 
whole. As a minimum, a new flexible coupling, bolts, and turning gear output shaft bolts and 
nuts are needed. The customer is also kindly requested to review the O&M instructions for 
this equipment with regards to greasing and other general maintenance.

check.

### 4.4.2 Stator Winding Resistance
R
M
Part Condition: Good
Part Description: 
DC resistance of a winding is a measure of abnormalities arising from loose connections, 
broken connections, high contact resistance at brazed joints. Interpretation of results is 
usually based on comparison of measurements made at site to data of tests carried out at 
factory or during previous tests/outages. Agreement within 2% of any of the above 
comparisons is usually considered satisfactory. Resistance being temperature sensitive, it is 
required to correct the resistance measurements to values corresponding to the reference 
temperature to be able to compare data (GE is using 25C as reference temperature).
The DC resistance was carried out using a Digital Low Resistance Ohmmeter (DLRO) which 
is measuring by applying a DC voltage and current through the winding. The resistance is 
the voltage divided by current. The test passed as the winding resistance is within the 
deviation tolerance from the factory value and within the deviation between each phase.

The Generator Condition  Monitor (GCM) is a sensitive real-time 
instrument designed to provide immediate indicat ion of overheat ing
in hydrogen-cooled generators before extensive damage canoccur. 
Tests conducted on operating hydrogen-cooled generators have 
shown that the GCM can detect thermal decomposition of small 
amounts of insulating materials.
Thermal decomposition of organic materials such as epoxy paint, 
core lamination enamel or other insulating materials used in the 
generator results in the production of a  large number  of small 
particles. The onset of particle production, as the material  is heated, 
occurs at a temperature characteristic of the material and its 
surrounding atmosphere.  Below this temperature,  no particles are 
created, yet once the critical temperature is reached, millions  of 
submicron  particles are generated each second for every square 
centimeter of surface.
GCM-X represents the next generation  in condition  monitoring -
incorporating microprocessor based electronics, flameproof, 
intrinsically safe design features (Ex  II H2, CE) and self diagnostics. 
E/One has taken the field-proven system that has served the 
worldwide power generation community for decades and improved 
upon it in the form of increased safety,  performance and reliability.

Component Replacement Instructions
The GCM-X was designed to facilitate component  replacement, when and if it becomes neces•
sary in the field. Several GCM-X components/assemblies may be removed by site personnel and 
forwarded to Environment One for evaluation  repair/replacement, as noted below.  In all other 
instances, the GCM-X will need to be returned to Environment One for servicing,  or an Environ• 
ment One technician will be required on site.
Plant management  is to assure that individuals performing work on the GCM-X are adequately
trained to do so and that they work in accordance with Cenelec requirements, local codes and 
generally accepted professional  practice.
If oil contamination  is suspected,  Environment One recommends that the GCM-X be returned for
comprehensive evaluation, cleaning and repair.
After the GCM-X has been installed and commissioned,  individuals  performing service
work on the electronics must wear an electrostatic wriststrap.
ICD, Filter Solenoid and Sampling System Solenoid
The Ion  Chamber Detector (ICD) (GD0013G04),  Filter Solenoid Assembly,  Sampling System 
Solenoid Assembly and GCM-X Heater (GA0363P01) are mounted on the GCM-X "mounting 
plate," which is an aluminum plate attached to the GCM-X frame by four 3/8-inch nuts. Removal
of any of the mounted components  is  best accomplished  by removing the back plate first and 
then removing the individual assembly.
To remove the mounting plate:
Disconnect power from the GCM-X.
Detach the heater from the mounting plate by removing the four screws on the heater's
mounting bracket.
Detach grounding wire and other cables from the four wire ties.
Detach solenoid coils from the two solenoid valves.
Detach tubing connections from assemblies  mounted to the mounting plate.
Remove the four 3/8-inch bolts that secure the mounting plate to the GCM-X frame.
Each of the respective components  mounted on the GCM-X back plate can then be removed for
service, replacement or return to Environment One. To re-install the assemblies, reverse the 
process above.
Processor Assembly
The Processor Assembly  is located  in the flameproof enclosure,  which is  referred to as the
System Electronics.  To remove the Controller Assembly:
1.   Disconnect power from the GCM-X.

Display Assembly
The Display Assembly  is located  behind the GCM-X subdoor, which is integral to the GCM-X
module assembly. To remove the Display Assembly:
1.
Disconnect  power from the GCM-X.
2.
Open the GCM-X front door.
3.
Open the GCM-X subdoor, which will enable access to the GCM-X Display Panel.
4.
Disconnect the 15-pin  D-connector from the back of the display board.
5.
Loosen the four display assembly  mounting screws located  on the back side of the GCM-X
module (support the display assembly with your other hand).
6.
Detach the grounding wire and remove the display assembly.

Fuses
The GCM-X contains a 2A slo-blo fuse that may be replaced by plant personnel. The fuse is
located on the 1/0 board,  adjacent to the power and heater connections.  It is labeled "F1."
Disconnect  power from the GCM-X.
Open the cover of the flameproof enclosure, taking care not to damage the surfaces.
Use a fuse puller to remove the fuse.
Replace fuse with  Littlefuse #218 002 or equivalent.
Replace flameproof enclosure  cover and secure.

Summary
To  inform  EX2100  users  of  a  fuse  replacement  
that  on large  static  exciter  systems  using  
100mm  SCRs  there  is  a potential fuse 
coordination issue. In the event of an SCR failure, 
the protective leg fuses may not clear (open) in 
time to prevent a unit trip.
TIL 1645 On  EX2100  100mm  warm-backup  
control  systems applied  on  units  with  an  amps  
field  full  load  (AFFL) rating  of  less  than  2050  
amps,  GE  recommends  the parallel 1200-amp  
DC  leg  fuses  be  replaced  with  two parallel 
800-amp  fuses.   These  fuses  will  isolate  a 
shorted  SCR  and  keep  the  redundant  system  
from tripping the turbine on units fed from an 
auxiliary bus.
And was Customer witness installing  guide &was 
successfully implemented .
TIL 1645

## 1.  Remove the glastic pieces that hold down the LEXAN
## 2.  Remove the LEXAN
## 3.  Remove thefour5/16inch bolts

PURPOSE
Leakage of the water-cooled bus has 
been detected in some static starters 
which have been in service for10 or more 
years. Such leakage may result in loss of 
coolant and inability to start the gas 
turbine. 
Leakage may further result in failure of 
the static starter with an arcing fault 
within the enclosure.
TIL 1755-R3

REASON FOR REVISION
Recommendation is revised to replace 
water-cooled bus based on ultrasonic testing
(UT) results (condition-based instead of 
interval-based).And was Customer witness 
installing  guide.
TIL 1755-R3

PREPARATION
LOTO and EHS
1-Follow site specific  LOTO and EHS procedures as 
applicable.
2.Shut down all power supplies to the static starter,  including  
control    and main  ac input and output.  LOTO on control  
power  breaker (CB1 ), generator disconnect  switch  (895S), 
and isolation  transformer switch  (525S),  89TS  and  89MD 
switch
3. Use appropriate  personal  protective equipment  (PPE).
4.Use local grounding spider on HY bus and using tic-tracer  
to verify zero volts.
TIL 1755-R3

Brief Modification / Changes on existing
1-perform an ultrasonic test (UT) on the accessible 
outer/rear side of the bus bar elbows through GE-
LES services.
2-Add six stainless steel straight flow restrictors in 
the load bridge.
3.Replace six nylon tee connectors with stainless 
steel flow restrictors in the source bridge.
4-Testing with customer.
TIL 1755-R3

1-We verify that the power LCI section in need of repair has been properly deenergized per the

2-We You will also need to separate the blue hoses at the Tee-junctions to remove the water- cooled

3- We replace six nylon tee connectors with stainless steel flow restrictors in the source bridge.
4-connect the blue hoses to the stainless-steel Tee flow restrictor to connect to the copper pipes. 
Refer Appendix B for flow restrictor installation
5-We add six stainless steel straight flow restrictors in the load bridge
6-Tighten the ends with two hose clamps per bus, ensuring that both hose clamps are tightened on 
the mouth of the pipe connection and not the hose itself.

3. Flush the LCI cooling water system:

all connections are placed and tightened.
b. Obtain at least 12 gallons (50 liters) of pure 100% demineralized water.

On 12 December 2020, Cairo North Power Plant started a planned Major Inspection (MI) for 
GT unit serial number 298464 and Generator 337X581 rotor out. 
GT:
Upon visual inspections and compressor mapping, findings were as follows:
1.      High corrosion pitting on compressor forward stages 0-5 (rotor and stator).
2.      R1-B28 with a dent with high risk of failure.
3.      Rust between the stators and casing on almost all stages causing difficult removal of 
stators.
4.      Tip rubs and edge damages on several stages at random.
Recommendation was to replace stators and rotor per ER case and findings to reduce the 
risk of failure due to the as found condition.
Disassembly of all components started on 12 December 2020, new HGP components were 
reassembled, and team demobilized on 17 January 2021 until new compressor stator 
(Package 5) parts arrival.
Team returned on 22 January 2021 to install new upgraded Package 5 stators and IGV 
parts. All upper half casings were reinstalled to avoid casing deformation.
The scope was put on-hold on 12 February 2021 where site team demobilized until rotor 
repair and return for reassembly. The damaged rotor was placed inside the shipping box on 
13 February to be ready for shipping.
The team returned on June 15 for the reassembly phase, new rotor was received from 
Nubaria Power Plant.
The new turbine rotor was installed and all combustion and HGP components were replaced 
with new/refurbished parts. GT lift oil flow control valves were replaced with new ones.
The lube oil tank was cleaned by the customer, and placed new oil into the tank.
Generator:
The generator field was planned for repair, the unit was disassembled, and the field was 
pulled out on 1 January 2021 and ready for shipping. The rotor was lifted and sent for 
shipment on 22 January 2021 due to delay of shipping arrangements. The stator and 
removed parts were tested and visually inspected, and ER case called for stator re-wedge.
GT and generator parts (bearings/buckets/new CI components, end shields, special tools 
etc.) were stored by the customer until return of the both rotors.
Upon stator re-wedge parts arrival, scope was implemented successfully and electrical 
testing was performed before and after the scope as documented in the below report to

Preparation/Timeline of Events:
- The team started to Mobilize / Move on Site on 12th of December 2020.
- Team demobilized on 17th of January 2021 after disassembly.
- Team mobilized again on 22nd of January 2021 for generator rotor shipping, installing new 
Package 5 parts, and boxing up unit without the rotor to avoid any deformation/damage due 
to weather.
- Team demobilized on 14th of February after placing the old GT rotor in shipping box, and 
completing site cleanup.
- Team re-mobilized to site on 15th of June 2021 for GT reassembly and Generator re-wedge 
scopes.
- Team demobilized 15th of July awaiting missing re-wedge parts/chemicals (stuck in 
customs clearance).
- Team re-mobilized to site on 12th of August to finalize Generator re-wedge scope, 
mechanical reassembly and startup of the unit.
- Unit started up successfully on 4th of September, reaching a baseload of 235 MW. 
Emissions tuning was also performed on the unit.
GE/FieldCore team provided technical direction and supervision of all the mechanical 
activities throughout the outage. The scope of work is documented throughout this report. 
The unit is operated and maintained by the customer. The craft labor was provided by 
customer.
All the electrical connections and mechanical equipment etc. necessary to complete the 
work safely under the LOTO procedure were disconnected/isolated by GE and the permit to 
work system was implemented. All components that were removed and replaced have been 
documented in this report.

1.      Fuel nozzles and liner caps.

4.      1st, 2nd and 3rd stage nozzles.
5.      1st, 2nd and 3rd stage shrouds.
6.      1st, 2nd and 3rd stage buckets.
7.      IGV blades, arm and actuator (package 5 upgrade).
8.      Compressor stator vanes (package 5 upgrade).
9.      Unit rotor.
10.    Bearings (GT bearing 2 oversized).
11.    GT lift oil hoses and flow control valves.

Part Condition: Good
Part Description: 
The filter house stripped down of old filters, cleaned and reassembled with new cylindrical 
and conical filters. Upon closeout inspection, minor damage to sheet metal on filters were 
noted and some mixed-and-matched elements from different manufacturers or batches of 
production. Comments on inadequate sealing have been corrected prior to operation.
The silencer duct and inlet plenum were entered for final inspection, noting clean and dry 
surfaces, intact probes, properly sealed expansion joints, and unchipped paint. Stud 
protrusion beyond the nut for the expansion joints were less than ideal, some just at the 
surface of the nut. The customer was advised to revise the quality and proper fill of the 
expansion joint on both the C-wall and air cone sides.

Part Description: 
The turning gear and SSS clutch assembly was decoupled, preserved, and returned to 
position. The axial location was marked with stoppers welded on the base plate in lieu of 
drilling new dowel pins.
Recommendation Status: Should be planned for next Outage
Recommendation Type: Parts
Recommendation Description: 
The turning gear assembly is one of the most important components of the GT train and is 
necessary for operation, particularly during startup and shutdown. Normal wear and age 
may soon affect the integrity of the system. The customer is recommended to have in store 
replacement parts for the worm gear, ratcheting device, SSS clutch, or the assembly as a 
whole. As a minimum, a new flexible coupling, bolts, and turning gear output shaft bolts and 
nuts are needed. The customer is also kindly requested to review the O&M instructions for 
this equipment with regards to greasing and other general maintenance.

Part Condition: Good
Part Description: 
DC resistance of a winding is a measure of abnormalities arising from loose connections, 
broken connections, high contact resistance at brazed joints. Interpretation of results is 
usually based on comparison of measurements made at site to data of tests carried out at 
factory or during previous tests/outages. Agreement within 2% of any of the above 
comparisons is usually considered satisfactory. Resistance being temperature sensitive, it is 
required to correct the resistance measurements to values corresponding to the reference 
temperature to be able to compare data (GE is using 25C as reference temperature).
The DC resistance was carried out using a Digital Low Resistance Ohmmeter (DLRO) which 
is measuring by applying a DC voltage and current through the winding. The resistance is 
the voltage divided by current. The test passed as the winding resistance is within the 
deviation tolerance from the factory value and within the deviation between each phase.

The Generator Condition  Monitor (GCM) is a sensitive real-time 
instrument designed to provide immediate indicat ion of overheat ing
in hydrogen-cooled generators before extensive damage canoccur. 
Tests conducted on operating hydrogen-cooled generators have 
shown that the GCM can detect thermal decomposition of small 
amounts of insulating materials.
Thermal decomposition of organic materials such as epoxy paint, 
core lamination enamel or other insulating materials used in the 
generator results in the production of a  large number  of small 
particles. The onset of particle production, as the material  is heated, 
occurs at a temperature characteristic of the material and its 
surrounding atmosphere.  Below this temperature,  no particles are 
created, yet once the critical temperature is reached, millions  of 
submicron  particles are generated each second for every square 
centimeter of surface.
GCM-X represents the next generation  in condition  monitoring -
incorporating microprocessor based electronics, flameproof, 
intrinsically safe design features (Ex  II H2, CE) and self diagnostics. 
E/One has taken the field-proven system that has served the 
worldwide power generation community for decades and improved 
upon it in the form of increased safety,  performance and reliability.

core lamination enamel or other insulating materials used in the 
generator results in the production of a  large number  of small 
particles. The onset of particle production, as the material  is heated, 
occurs at a temperature characteristic of the material and its 
surrounding atmosphere.  Below this temperature,  no particles are 
created, yet once the critical temperature is reached, millions  of 
submicron  particles are generated each second for every square 
centimeter of surface.
GCM-X represents the next generation  in condition  monitoring -
incorporating microprocessor based electronics, flameproof, 
intrinsically safe design features (Ex  II H2, CE) and self diagnostics. 
E/One has taken the field-proven system that has served the 
worldwide power generation community for decades and improved 
upon it in the form of increased safety,  performance and reliability.

Component Replacement Instructions
The GCM-X was designed to facilitate component  replacement, when and if it becomes neces•
sary in the field. Several GCM-X components/assemblies may be removed by site personnel and 
forwarded to Environment One for evaluation  repair/replacement, as noted below.  In all other 
instances, the GCM-X will need to be returned to Environment One for servicing,  or an Environ• 
ment One technician will be required on site.
Plant management  is to assure that individuals performing work on the GCM-X are adequately
trained to do so and that they work in accordance with Cenelec requirements, local codes and 
generally accepted professional  practice.
If oil contamination  is suspected,  Environment One recommends that the GCM-X be returned for
comprehensive evaluation, cleaning and repair.
After the GCM-X has been installed and commissioned,  individuals  performing service
work on the electronics must wear an electrostatic wriststrap.
ICD, Filter Solenoid and Sampling System Solenoid
The Ion  Chamber Detector (ICD) (GD0013G04),  Filter Solenoid Assembly,  Sampling System 
Solenoid Assembly and GCM-X Heater (GA0363P01) are mounted on the GCM-X "mounting 
plate," which is an aluminum plate attached to the GCM-X frame by four 3/8-inch nuts. Removal
of any of the mounted components  is  best accomplished  by removing the back plate first and 
then removing the individual assembly.
To remove the mounting plate:
Disconnect power from the GCM-X.
Detach the heater from the mounting plate by removing the four screws on the heater's
mounting bracket.
Detach grounding wire and other cables from the four wire ties.
Detach solenoid coils from the two solenoid valves.
Detach tubing connections from assemblies  mounted to the mounting plate.
Remove the four 3/8-inch bolts that secure the mounting plate to the GCM-X frame.
Each of the respective components  mounted on the GCM-X back plate can then be removed for
service, replacement or return to Environment One. To re-install the assemblies, reverse the 
process above.
